label: final copy step of length-3 sequences
explanation: Active almost only in the copy phase of the shortest (L=3) sequences: 94% of activation mass is on L=3, the rest mostly L=4. It fires on about 80% of L=3 final steps (t=5, output orig(2), input orig(1), two steps after <DEL>), and that step holds 84% of the mass. It also fires more weakly on about 30% of L=3 t=4 steps (the first fed-back token); I could not find what decides which ones. Magnitude is largest at the L=3 final step. The input token p gives the strongest activations (5x lift, every top example). Repeated tokens (in_count>=2) damp it. It never fires in the original or delimiter phase, never on the first occurrence of a token, and almost never for L>=5. (L==3)&(phase==2) catches 94% of mass but at 0.55 precision.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: p, o, 2, 1, 3, f; least: n, s, l, w) and the previous input (most: 0, g, i, 2, y, a; least: m, t, z, x); timing cues that raise it most: L=3, L=3 & t=5, L=3 & t=4.
